_note: Gating the quality ladder's locks on whether its own prediction can be trusted. The ladder default was turned on in c9d36df on the strength of a zero-regression sweep over the GATED SIXTEEN; parity-expanded-2026-08-05d then measured the same flip over the 29-document expansion corpus and found four candidate-side regressions and a degraded reference arm. `before` here is c9d36df (ladder on, ungated) and `after` is the same tree with `_lockable_text` and the page-height budget in `ladder.apply_ladder`. -05c is the pre-flip reference point and is the TARGET, not a floor: acceptance was that the regressions return to it while c1/c4/l1's gains hold. Raw sweep at docs/evidence/parity-expanded-2026-08-05e.json.
_the_lesson: A CHANGE TO A DEFAULT THAT EVERY DOCUMENT FLOWS THROUGH IS MEASURED ON BOTH CORPORA BEFORE IT LANDS, NEVER ON THE GATED SIXTEEN ALONE. The gate is not a sample of the world; it is sixteen documents that happen to be pinned. c9d36df passed it with zero regressions and was still wrong about four expansion documents.

diagnosis._note: Two independent failures, both of them locks the ladder was confident about. Attribution was measured by ablation (ladder / figure-merge / both): the figure-merge change from c9d36df is innocent on every affected document -- `merge` equals `none` on x01, x06, x10, x11 and x12 -- so every expansion regression is the ladder's.

A_metric_blindness.finding: `_predictable` checked that the font FAMILY maps to a base-14 name and never that the CHARACTERS are in that font's WinAnsi repertoire. The metrics do not approximate the missing scripts, they do not see them, and they return a number anyway.

representability_probe._note: Same-script narrow vs wide, 10 characters, tiro 11pt. Latin resolves glyph by glyph; Cyrillic and Greek return a constant.

A_metric_blindness.why_not_simply_representability: c4_i18n's CJK is equally invisible and locking it moved within2pt 0.1966 -> 0.5043. CJK is written WITHOUT SPACES, so the renderer breaks it wherever its own measurement lands and cannot reproduce the source's break by luck; and the metric error is uniform across the run, so a width fraction still maps onto the right character. Cyrillic and Greek break at spaces exactly like Latin, so the renderer already reproduces the source wrap and a lock can only disturb it. The rule is therefore: measured text, OR a script continuum. Not representability.
A_metric_blindness.tolerance: UNMEASURED_MAX_FRAC = 0.05. l1_word_native's list paragraph carries two U+F0B7 Wingdings bullets among ~200 Latin characters; an all-or-nothing test vetoed it and cost word_recall 1.0 -> 0.9931 for nothing. x06's Cyrillic body is 71% of its paragraph.

B_page_height.finding: A lock pins the source's line count. Where the renderer would have used fewer lines, that is TALLER -- and in free flow it pushes pages over. In a table cell the row height is declared by the source and restoring it is the entire point.
B_page_height.exhibit: x10_chrome_tables_plain: the same two locks improved dy_p50 17.2 -> 1.65 and within2pt 0.015 -> 0.0991 while taking the document 2/2 -> 2/3 pages and word_recall 0.9963 -> 0.8657. The placement was right and the page could not hold it.
B_page_height.rule: PAGE_SLACK_FRAC = 0.25, applied to the height REMAINING AFTER the lock so a page full of candidates cannot accept them one at a time. Table cells are exempt.

slack_against_outcome._note: Page slack as a fraction of capacity, against whether locking that page helped.

lock_census_both_corpora._note: infer + ladder over all 45 fixtures, no rendering. Every refusal is now named in `ladder.summarise` rather than folded into an unexplained denominator.

gated16._note: testkit/runall.py both lanes, canonical container. IDENTICAL to the baseline recorded in c9d36df, to every digit -- the gating removes no gated gain. Gate PASS both lanes with zero findings; NO re-record was needed or performed.

expansion_candidate._note: testkit/parity_expansion.py --profile candidate, all 29 documents, 795s. Three-way: -05c is the target. `now` equal to -05c is the acceptance condition; better than -05c is a retained gain.

x01_lo_memo_pageno.pdf._note: x01 never regressed in absolute terms. Its -05d verdict flip was 'reference improved' -- the pymupdf arm gained more than pdfium and widened the parity gap. Both arms are better than -05c.

y_series_page_err._note: The page-count drift, which was the -05d y-series finding. Residual +4 across eight documents, against -05d's +26.

expansion_candidate.sub_noise_residuals: Several y-series dy_p50 and doc_recall values differ from -05c in the third decimal (y02 dy 57.98 -> 57.99, y08 doc_recall 0.9691 -> 0.9683, y13 dy 38.46 -> 38.5). These are documents rendering 160-350 pages against a 46-126 page source, where the metric is dominated by gross page displacement; hundredths of a point are not a signal.

gated16_candidate_parity._note: backend_parity.py --profile candidate. The -05d 'l1_word_native NEW gated-candidate MAJOR' is a parity-framing artifact, not a quality loss, and this records why so it is not re-chased.

l1_word_native.pdf.reading: BOTH arms improved enormously -- candidate 24.59 -> 9.89 and reference 34.99 -> 8.49. The verdict went MAJOR only because the reference improved FASTER. Returning this document to its -05c verdict would mean discarding a 25pt placement gain on both backends, which is not a repair.

c4_i18n.pdf._note: Its live_text_cov gap (reference 1.0, candidate 0.9091) is identical in -05c and -05d: a long-standing pdfium rasterisation difference, not caused here.
c4_i18n.pdf.reading: Better than -05c, slightly below -05d: the page-height budget declines two locks the ungated ladder took in the pdfium arm.

y10_nist_fips180_reference_arm._note: THE ONE ACCEPTANCE ITEM NOT MET. Reported rather than fixed, because the obvious fix is blocked on a decision I must not take alone.
y10_nist_fips180_reference_arm.isolation: pymupdf/gdocs/none/refine0, ladder off vs on: pages 36/43 -> 36/44, dy_p50 49.56 -> 58.97, word_recall 0.4872 -> 0.3238. One extra page early in a 43-page document puts everything after it on the wrong page, which is the whole of the recall loss.
y10_nist_fips180_reference_arm.mechanism: Five locks survive both gates, and none of them is wrapped prose. Two are tab-separated fragments ('(i)\t(i) j 0'); one has a second source line 6.0pt wide; two have interior line widths varying by 180-280pt ([161.5, 434.3, 250.8, 345.4] and [190.3, 470.9, 470.8, 470.8, 128.3]). These are definition lists and symbol tables that `infer` flattened into paragraphs, and the width-fraction cut model has no meaning on them.
y10_nist_fips180_reference_arm.candidate_fix: Require the INTERIOR source line widths (dropping the first, which may be a merged heading, and the last, which is always short) to be uniform -- wrapped prose has interior lines at the column width by construction.
y10_nist_fips180_reference_arm.why_not_landed: Measured: that test also refuses l1_word_native's bullet-list paragraph (widths [41.5, 217.2, 284.2, 284.7], interior spread 67pt), which drops l1's word_recall from 1.0 to 0.9931. testkit/gate_baseline.json records l1 word_recall 1.0 in BOTH lanes, so the fix regresses the gate against a baseline this task was instructed not to re-record. Trading a gated document's recall for an expansion document's is an adjudication, not an implementation detail.
